description: ``write_guard._normalize_path`` called ``os.path.expanduser(file_path)`` without type-checking. Any non-str ``file_path`` (``int``, ``null``, ``list``, ``dict``, ``bool``) raised ``TypeError`` which bubbled to ``SystemExit(main())`` → exit 1. Per the Claude Code hook protocol (``docs/external/cc-hook-protocol.md``), exit 1 is a non-blocking script error — the tool call proceeds. Reproduction: ``echo '{"tool_input":{"file_path":42,"content":"x"}}' | python3 .../write_guard.py`` returned exit 1 with a Python traceback on stderr, fail-open. Fix: ``check_write_edit`` checks ``isinstance(file_path, str)`` before normalization and returns ``deny()`` for non-str payloads; ``_normalize_path`` adds a defense-in-depth ``<invalid>`` sentinel; ``main()`` wraps the body in ``try/except BaseException`` returning ``deny()`` so any other uncaught crash also fails-closed.
documented_in: tests/test_hooks.py::TestWriteGuardTypeCoercion (8 tests covering int/null/list/dict/bool plus the BaseException umbrella for non-str Bash command)
